topics.title: How Do We Learn About the Past?

concepts.learning_objective: Explain what history is and how human history fits within the Earth's very long history.
Identify what geologists, palaeontologists, anthropologists and archaeologists study.

topics.title: How Is Time Measured in History?

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Gregorian calendar, its leap-year rule and the meaning of CE and BCE.
Calculate the number of years between BCE and CE dates, keeping in mind that there is no year zero.

topics.title: Timelines, Centuries, Millenniums and Indian Calendars

concepts.learning_objective: Use a timeline to arrange dates and events in chronological order.
Work out which century or millennium, CE or BCE, a given year belongs to.
State what a panchanga is and what information it provides.

topics.title: What Are the Sources of History?

concepts.learning_objective: Define a source of history and recognise different kinds of sources.
Explain why historians compare many sources and decide which to trust when they disagree.
Identify the experts and scientific studies that help reconstruct the past.
Describe how early humans lived as hunters and gatherers in bands.
Explain what rock paintings, tools and ornaments tell us about early humans.

topics.title: The First Crops and Growing Communities

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the end of the last Ice Age led to settled farming near rivers.
Trace how farming communities grew into villages and towns with new technologies.
